voyage.name: Tomb of Priscilla
voyage.content: A 1st-century tomb surrounded by two farmhouses from the Middle Ages, one of which used to be a cheese store. Rather hidden behind a high wall, the tomb is rarely open to the public. You might be lucky on a Sunday: on the third Sunday of every month there is a guided tour at 11:00.

voyage.name: Chapel of Reginald Pole
voyage.content: A strange building, constructed by Reginald Pole, an English cardinal and later Archbishop of Canterbury, allegedly on the spot where he was able to escape from assassins sent by the English King Henry VIII.

voyage.name: The Catacombs of San Callisto
voyage.price: €8, includes a guided tour in several languages
voyage.content: Although started in the 2nd century, San Callisto has had many more recent burials, including 16 popes. The burial arcades are almost 20 km long.

voyage.name: The Catacombs of San Domitilla
voyage.content: The Catacombs of Domitilla are considered to be the best preserved of all Roman catacombs. They are the only ones still to contain bones. Domitilla also has a subterranean basilica, much of which was reconstructed in 1870.

voyage.name: Basilica and catacombs of San Sebastiano
voyage.content: The first basilica was constructed in the 4th century and dedicated to San Sebastian, a martyr of the 3rd century. Sebastian's remains were transferred to St. Peter's in 826, prior to a Saracen assault when the church was destroyed. The current church was largely constructed in the 17th-century. Until the Great Jubilee in 2000 this was one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches of Rome, i.e. the churches that all Roman Cathol

voyage.name: Fosse Ardeatine
voyage.content: This was the site of the slaughter in 1944 of 335 Italians, including many Jews from the Ghetto, in retaliation for a Partisan attack on German troops in Rome. The caves where the massacre took place are now a National Monument and Memorial Cemetery and can be visited daily.

voyage.name: Jewish Catacombs
voyage.content: These are underneath a property known as Vigna Randanini. The catacombs are much smaller than the Christian catacombs and much less easy to visit. Groups are limited to twelve people at any one time and you need to take your own lighting!

voyage.name: Caffarella Park
voyage.content: Caffarella Park covers an area of 339 ha and is part of the larger Appia Antica park. It contains both a working farm and numerous Roman ruins, some quite well preserved and is a great place for a stroll or cycle away from Rome’s traffic.

voyage.name: Circus of Maxentius
voyage.content: This well-preserved Roman circus was built at the beginning of the fourth century. It was part of an imperial villa built by Maxentius and the complex also contains the Mausoleum of his son, Romolo.

voyage.name: Tomb of Cecilia Metella
voyage.price: A €5 ticket gives admission to the tomb and to Villa dei Quintili, valid for 2 days
voyage.hours: From 09:00, variable closing depending on time of year
voyage.content: The mausoleum of Cecilia Metella, who died in 69 BC, is the best preserved monument on the Appian Way and dominates the surroundings. In the Middle Ages it was transformed into a fortress and battlements were added. At that time there was considerable competition for ownership because of its strategic location.

voyage.name: Capo di Bove
voyage.content: This archaeological site displays the thermal baths of the villa of the wealthy Herod Atticus. Also in the complex is a restored villa, until 2002 a private residence, that has an exterior completely covered with pieces from Roman ruins, including pipes used in the baths. There are some very helpful staff to show you around, although they only speak Italian. An interesting photographic exhibition in the house traces

voyage.name: Villa dei Quintilii
voyage.price: A €5 ticket gives admission to the villa, to Santa Maria Nova, and to Cecilia Metella
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-19:00 or sunset, whichever is earlier
voyage.content: This impressive villa covers 23 hectares. It can be accessed from the Via Appia Nuova (Bus 118) or through Via Appia Antica 251. Parts can be seen from the Appian Way at around the 5th mile just after No 251. The villa was built by Maximus and Condinus Quintilii. The emperor Commudus liked it so much that he put the brothers to death in 182 AD and took it for himself. A museum has friezes and sculptures from the vill

voyage.name: Casal Rotondo
voyage.content: Casal Rotondo is the biggest mausoleum on the Appian Way, at about the sixth mile. It now incorporates a small private villa, originally a farmhouse. It is not known for whom it was built. The wall of fragments next to it, constructed by Luigi Canina, has ruins referring to the Cotta family but this family is now believed to not be associated with the Casal Rotondo.

voyage.name: Parco degli Acquedotti (Aqueduct Park)
voyage.address: between Via Appia Nuova and Via Tuscolana
voyage.content: This pleasant park contains very well-preserved ruins of two aqueducts and some of the original surface of the Roman Via Latina. Gets crowded on Sundays but almost empty the rest of the week during term time. Good place for joggers.

voyage.name: Abbey of the three fountains (Abazzia delle tre fontane)
voyage.content: A truly quiet oasis close to the hustle and bustle of EUR. There are three churches in this complex and the doors are open all day, unlike city churches. The monks produce a range of products such as liqueurs, chocolate and honey, as well as a cure for the illnesses Romans suffer when the Scirocco wind blows in from the Sahara. These are on sale at a shop at the Abbey.

voyage.name: L. Pigorini National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography
voyage.content: An ethnographic collection of around 60,000 pieces from European indigenous cultures. Documents evolution from the Palaeolithic age to the Iron Age.

voyage.name: Museo della Civilta Romana (Museum of Rome's Civilization)
voyage.hours: Closed due to redevelopment of the building
voyage.address: Piazza G. Agnelli (close to the Pigorini museum)
voyage.content: Perhaps most famous for a large model of imperial Rome, but also has a large display of various aspects of ancient Rome, using plaster casts, models and reconstructions of works found in museums throughout the world.

voyage.name: Rome's Planetarium
voyage.content: Regular shows plus an excellent astronomical museum.

voyage.name: Square Colosseum
voyage.alt: Colosseo Quadrato, also known as Palazzo della Civiltà Italiana
voyage.content: Constructed around the 1940s as the centrepiece of the EUR, but unused for a long time. It was restored before 2015 when the luxury fashion label Fendi moved in.

voyage.name: San Paolo fuori le Mura
voyage.content: Also known as St Paul Outside the Walls. This is on the outskirts of Rome in an otherwise drab modern neighborhood. The enormous basilica is a faithful reconstruction, finished in 1854, of the ancient basilica which burned down in 1823. Parts of the original interior were rescued from the fire and have been extensively restored. Visiting in the afternoon may avoid the tourist coaches. Don't miss the medieval cloister

voyage.name: Santa Passera
voyage.content: This church can be an interesting deviation if you are passing through its neighbourhood. It is believed to be the grave of the Saints Ciro and Giovanni, killed during the time of the Emperor Diocletian. The original name was Abba Cyrus and through Appaciro and then Appacero it finally became Pacera, very close to today's Passera. The building is on top of a 3rd century building still visible in the lower floor and i

voyage.name: Centrale Montemartini Museum
voyage.price: €4.50 plus extra fees for special exhibits
voyage.content: This delightful museum provides an interesting juxtaposition between the buildings and equipment of Rome's first electricity generating plant and the exhibits, which are mainly from excavations of Roman sites. A combined ticket with the museums on the Capitoline Hill provides big reductions.

voyage.name: Sanctuary of Divino Amore.
voyage.content: This is an important place of pilgrimage for Catholics because of the supposedly miraculous powers of an image of the Virgin Mary. The first miracle was in 1740 when a traveller being attacked by a pack of dogs called out to the Virgin’s image for rescue and the dogs calmed down. The image was moved to Rome in the Second World War and is credited with saving the city from destruction, as a result of which Romans vowe

voyage.name: Jubilee Church
voyage.content: A modern church designed by the world-famous architect Richard Meier. Completed in 2003 and built as a project to socially revive the surrounding Tor Tre Teste area.

voyage.name: Bike
voyage.content: Rent a bike and explore the many remains of the Appian Way park area.

voyage.name: Al peperoncino
voyage.content: This pizzeria has a good Roman style pizza (the thin one) and also a good choice of fried vegetables and appetizers. Price is low to mid-range, food quality and service are medium.

voyage.name: Gelato di San Crispino
voyage.content: One of the best ice cream makers in Rome. From humble beginnings here, San Crispino has expanded and you can now buy special packs at Fiumicino airport to take home with you. Pure ingredients; good selection of fruit sorbets (flavours according to the season) and ice creams.

voyage.name: Le Bistrot
voyage.content: Creative French and vegetarian cuisine with a very kind staff and a homey environment. Better to reserve.

voyage.name: Mama Che Pizza
voyage.content: Worth stopping by if you're close to the EUR and it's cheap. They also own the deli right next to it, where you can also get miniature pizzas and breads.

voyage.name: Trattoria Zampagna
voyage.content: Good Roman fare. One of the owners can speak English so that's helpful. Many interesting varieties of pasta along with traditional main courses such as ox tail. The owner has been known to take the time to introduce each of the dishes on the menu to the guests.

voyage.name: Martini Bed
voyage.content: Eco- & bike-friendly guesthouse. Twin, double, triple, quadruple and quintuple room with WiFi, air conditioning, safe, ensuite or private external bathroom, and self catering kitchen use. Cheap single rooms with shared bathroom. 24/7 self service breakfast included. Guarded parking. Bike rent.

voyage.name: Hotel Caravel
voyage.content: Cheap hotel: a bit off the beaten track but there are good bus connections.

voyage.name: Hotel Capanelle
voyage.content: Convenient for the Appian Way park and if you want to go to the races at Capannelle horse track. Short walk from Parco degli Aquedotti and Villa dei Quintili. Easily reached if you are coming from the south by car. Well-rated hotel but you will have to rely on an infrequent shuttle or public transport if you want to use it as a base for exploring downtown Rome.

voyage.name: Hotel EUR American Palace Rome
voyage.price: Around €130 for a double booked by internet. Ignore the ridiculously low prices displayed on the Home Page
voyage.content: This 4-star hotel has been refurbished to offer large and well decorated bedrooms.

voyage.name: Excel Hotel Ciampino Rome
voyage.content: Via Appia Nuova, 160, Marino. 4-star hotel just south of Ciampino Airport with 76 bedrooms of different size, private bathroom, spa centre, business services, restaurant, free shuttle to Ciampino airport and breakfast buffet. Double: €53 Triple: €59.

voyage.name: Villa EUR
voyage.content: Very quiet and stylish in midst of a park. You can reach it from the subway by a 5-min walk. The hotel has a small bar, excellent breakfast and a restaurant. In the vicinity of the hotel you can find an excellent restaurant La Taverna de Porto if you want to go out eating. There is also a tennis court, a gymnasium and even an Aikido Dojo.

voyage.name: Hotel Abitart
voyage.content: A "boutique" hotel that really merits the name. You'll have to stay in one of the eight themed suites to get the full effect but the whole hotel is covered with works of art of a surrealist nature, with considerable homage paid to Rene Magritte.

voyage.name: Trevi Fountain
voyage.content: Completed in 1762 to a design by Nicola Salvi, this spectacular Baroque fountain features a mythological sculptural composition of Neptune, god of the sea, flanked by two Tritons: one Triton labours to control a violent sea-horse, the other controls a pacified creature, both symbolising the dual nature of the world's oceans. The location of the Trevi fountain marks the terminus of the ancient Aqua Virgo aqueduct, com

voyage.name: Via Veneto
voyage.content: It was immortalised in 1960 by the Federico Fellini film La Dolce Vita. It is also the location of the US Embassy, in the massive Palazzo Margherita. Via Veneto went into a period of decline in the 1980s but has returned to popularity and the roadside cafes are the place to be seen if you are into that sort of thing.

voyage.name: Servian walls
voyage.content: Remains of the first city walls, built in the early 4th century BC and attributed to king Servius Tullius.

voyage.name: Capuchin Monastery
voyage.content: Built after 1631, the crypt of the church contains a macabre display - a series of chapels decorated with the bones of 3700 dead friars. The bones are glued to the walls and ceilings in bizarre and striking decorations.

voyage.name: Le Quattro Fontane
voyage.address: Intersection of Via delle Quattro Fontane and Via del Quirinale
voyage.content: Four fountains from the time of Pope Sixtus V when much of Rome was redeveloped. A reclining deity is the theme of each sculpture. This is a busy intersection and if you don't look twice you may miss these exquisite examples of Roman mythology.

voyage.name: Palazzo Massimo
voyage.price: €15 standard adult, €2 EU citizens between ages 18 and 24. This gives access to all four National Roman Museums in a 7-day period. Higher prices are charged when there are special exhibitions
voyage.content: A magnificent collection of ancient Roman sculptures, mosaics and wall paintings, including the famous paintings from the Imperial-era villa discovered under the Villa Farnesina, as well as the dining room from the Empress Livia's villa at Prima Porta. Located across the piazza from Termini, opposite the Baths of Diocletian.

voyage.name: Rome's National Museum at the Baths of Diocletian
voyage.price: €7 standard adult, €3.50 EU citizens between ages 18 and 24. This gives access to all four National Roman Museums in a 4-day period. Higher prices are charged when there are special exhibitions
voyage.content: On the site of the Roman baths this museum houses an enormous collection of statues, etc.

voyage.name: Palazzo Barberini
voyage.price: €5, several discounts available. Free entrance for people under 18 and over 65
voyage.content: This remarkable building, designed partly by Bernini, houses the National Gallery of Ancient Art, and includes some famous paintings by Filippo Lippi and Caravaggio, as well as Raphael's "La Fornarina".

voyage.name: Piazza Barberini
voyage.content: With Bernini's famous Triton Fountain. Via Veneto starts here too.

voyage.name: Palazzo del Quirinale
voyage.price: Artistic-Institutional itinerary €1.50; Thematic itinerary €10.00; Reservation in 5 days at least is mandatory which is made: online, by phone or at the Inforpoint (Salita di Montecavallo 15)
voyage.content: Home of the President of the Italian Republic, and the Quirinal Gardens. Built in 1573 as a papal summer residence, and has since also served as the residence for the pope and later for the king of Italy.

voyage.name: San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane
voyage.content: A very small and beautiful church, the first design commission of Francesco Borromini.

voyage.name: Santa Maria degli Angeli
voyage.content: This church was built inside the former baths of Diocletian. Very light and airy inside. Note the unusual art on the outside doors. Around solar noon check out the sun's image on Francesco Bianchini's meridian line inside.

voyage.name: Santa Maria della Vittoria
voyage.content: Now invaded by readers of Dan Brown's Angels and Demons, this is an interesting Baroque church containing Bernini's "Ecstasy of St. Teresa". Either side of this chapel are characters in what can best be described as theatre boxes. These are members of the Cornaro family, who paid for Bernini's sculpture. (As of Feb 2015, not visible due to restoration work.)

voyage.name: St Paul's Within the Walls
voyage.content: More modern than most Roman churches: it was not started until 1873. This is Rome’s Episcopalian church. Some very interesting artwork, particularly the mosaics by Edward Burne-Jones of the Pre-Raphaelite school.

voyage.name: British Embassy
voyage.content: At the northern end of Via XX Settembre next to the Porta Pia designed by Michaelangelo. The previous embassy had been destroyed by a terrorist bomb in 1946 and was eventually replaced by this world-renowned modern design by Sir Basil Spence. It was built on stilts so as not to interrupt the view of the garden.

voyage.name: Palazzo Colonna
voyage.price: €12 (includes optional guided tour); additional tour to the apartment of Princess Isabelle (when available) €15; extra tour to the terraced garden on the Quirinal hill (weather permitting) €10
voyage.hours: Sat 09:00-13:15; guided tour in English is at 12:00
voyage.content: One of the most splendid (still private) Baroque grand palaces in Rome.

voyage.name: Palazzo delle Esposizioni
voyage.price: €12.50; reductions €10. You can purchase a discounted, combined ticket for the Palazzo and the Scuderie.
voyage.content: Rotating exhibitions, usually three at one time. Exhibition descriptions normally provided in both Italian and English. Avoid Sunday morning, when the Romans go, as queues to get in can be long.

voyage.name: Scuderie del Quirinale
voyage.content: Former stables of the Quirinal Palace, now an exhibition centre that usually hosts some excellent art shows.

voyage.name: Limon'è
voyage.content: A shop that is all about lemons. You can buy products made with lemons: biscuits, jam, pasta, even soap, and of course limoncello. During hot days, do pop in for a glass of lemonade made with freshly pressed lemons or gelato where you can choose among a dozen of flavors each including lemon. The gelato is served in a lemon shell where the juice has just been pressed out to make lemonade!

voyage.name: Africa Restaurant
voyage.content: Eritrian

voyage.name: Piccolo Arancio
voyage.content: Small restaurant with a lot of Italian guests (but they are tourists, not Romans...) and moderate prices.

voyage.name: Il Gelato di San Crispino
voyage.content: Considered one of the best ice creams in Rome. Check out the meringue ice creams and the fruit sorbets according to the season.

voyage.name: Gelato g Italiano
voyage.content: An excellent ice-cream, one minute walk from Fontana di Trevi

voyage.name: Dagnino Tea Room, Galleria
voyage.content: If you haven't tried a "Cannolo" or a "Cassatina" then get one here, they are simply great. Don't sit at the tables (it's pretty expensive) just take them away. Good pastries too.

voyage.name: Harrys Bar
voyage.content: You can't visit Via Veneto and not go to Harrys Bar, forever associated with Fellinis' La Dolce Vita. Harrys is now a swanky upmarket {read expensive} bar/eatery where celebs can still be spotted. A piano bar. Sometimes guest artists availed themselves of the piano and entertain the patrons. For example, Australian Pianist Fiona Cohn played there.

voyage.name: Druid’s Rock Pub
voyage.content: The sister pub of the Druid’s Den.

voyage.name: Alessandro Hostels
voyage.content: Other branch: Alessandro Downtown, Via C. Cattaneo 23. 2nd Floor, +39 06 443 40 147. All locations are 5 minutes on foot from Termini, include free breakfast, free linens, no curfew, cheap internet, video security, free pizza parties at the Palace pub, internet PCs & Wi-Fi available at both hostels.

voyage.name: Domus Castrense Guest House Rome
voyage.price: €75 for a double room breakfast included
voyage.content: Single, double and triple bedrooms with private bath, TV LCD, breakfast, internet connection, telephone and mini bar for this guest house of Rome.

voyage.name: Evergreen B&B
voyage.content: No curfew, no lock-out. Towels and bed linen included. Daily room cleaning. English and Italian spoken.

voyage.name: Freedom Traveller Hostel
voyage.price: From €23 per night, including free breakfast, internet and dinner
voyage.content: A four-minute walk from the central train station, this hostel has adequate dorms, some have nice balconies. Kitchens and communal areas. No curfew, but lockout from 11:00 - 15:00.

voyage.name: Hotel Bed in Roma
voyage.content: 8 guest rooms which can be booked as single, double, twin, triple and family. All with en-suite services and shower. Special discounts with the local bars for breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Cortorillo Rome
voyage.price: Single and double rooms available starting from €40-€50 with breakfast included
voyage.content: Two-star hotel with 14 bedrooms divided in single, double and triple, and a single family room with four beds.

voyage.name: Hotel Indipendenza Rome
voyage.content: 3-star hotel. Single, double, twin, triple and family rooms available. All with en-suites services, LCD TV and free internet access.

voyage.name: Holiday Rome B&B
voyage.price: Price from €45 x person x night
voyage.content: Bed & Breakfast near Termini. Three rooms with private bathrooms and an air-conditioning system.

voyage.name: Hotel Rubino Rome
voyage.content: Cheap and cheerful low budget hotel right in the centre of Rome near the train station and public transport, caters mainly to young people. Clean and secure.

voyage.name: Inn Central Rome
voyage.content: Besides the single, double and triple rooms, this guest house of Rome also presents a cosy independent mini apartment for four people with kitchen facilities. Alla accommodations come with private bathroom. Single room: €60. Mini apartment: €95.

voyage.name: M&J Place Hostel Roma
voyage.content: Within spitting distance of the train station. Friendly staff, reasonable dorms and nice private room. This popular hostel has a good breakfast for €3 but no lockout or curfew. Try the bar Living Room for food or nice drinks. Free Wi-fi, tours, and free Mmps

voyage.name: Hotel Sonya
voyage.content: The Hotel Sonya is a three-star hotel in the centre of Rome, a few minutes away from Rome Termini Station and in front of the Opera House.

voyage.name: Anakin Stargate Hotel
voyage.price: Bed in a dormitory costs €22 including breakfast
voyage.content: 5 minutes away by foot from the termini central station, near the Castro Pretorio metro stop.

voyage.name: YWCA Rome
voyage.price: Base price excluding tourist tax and membership: €22 per person per night for a bed in a 4-person room. €33 to 38.50 EUR for a double, €55 for a private room (May 2023)
voyage.content: This youth hostel is part of the association of the World YWCA (Young Women Christian Association). It is found four blocks from Termini on the Via C. Balbo. A place fallen out of time, since not listed on the typical platforms and offering fixed rates even when everything else is booked (May 2023). You can stay there as a man too, just fill out the booking request form correctly. Breakfast is included, extra fees fo

voyage.name: Alex Inn
voyage.content: Small guest house in the centre of Rome near Via Veneto. Relatively new and pretty good facilities, and a small terrace off each room.

voyage.name: Al Viminale Hill & Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel on Colle Viminale near Termini Station. Offers its guests 15 rooms with Jacuzzi tub.

voyage.name: Art and Relax Suites Rome
voyage.content: The Art and Relax Suites is a cosy bed and breakfast of Rome with 6 double bedrooms with private en-suite services, shower and breakfast.

voyage.name: B&B Trevi Rome
voyage.content: The Trevi Rome is a bed and breakfast with 14 guest rooms divided in double and twin, standard and superior. A third bed available if needed. Rate for a double room €120.

voyage.name: Hotel Atlantico
voyage.content: A four-star hotel in a 1912 building on the highest of Rome's seven hills, the Esquilino, giving it good views of the city.

voyage.name: Hotel Cortina Rome
voyage.content: Three-star hotel of the central street of Via Nazionale with 14 bedrooms divided in single, double, twin, triple and quadruple with private bath (shower included). Also available two apartments 20 metres away from the hotel. €95 for a single and €115 for a double.

voyage.name: Hotel I Giardini del Quirinale
voyage.content: Upscale B&B very close to Via Nazionale and the Presidential Palace of Quirinale. All the bedrooms offer internet connection, mini bar, air conditioning, telephone with direct line and LCD television. Also available private parking and continental breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Martini Rome
voyage.content: The Martini is a three-star hotel of Rome with a large choice of bedrooms divided in single, double, triple and family; all equipped with private bathroom and bathtub. Double rooms: €160 with included breakfast.

voyage.name: Hotel Romanico Palace
voyage.content: A four-star hotel with 64 rooms divided between six floors, on the 7th floor there is a nice 360-degree panoramic terrace with good views of historical centre.

voyage.name: La Piccola Maison
voyage.content: Guest house in Via Veneto. Rooms with international channels, air conditioning, wifi, minifridge and telephone.

voyage.name: Nuovo Hotel Quattro Fontane
voyage.content: A 3-star hotel housed in an entirely renovated 18th-century palace.

voyage.name: Residence At Rome
voyage.price: The average price for a double is €220 per day
voyage.content: A guest house on the third floor in a residential building on Piazza Barberini, so the name holds true. No elevator available, and it's a long walk up the stairs with your luggage. There are 8 rooms with en-suite services divided in double, triple and suites, but there are no common rooms or amenities. You are paying for a room and that's all, some have complained about missing air-conditioning during the day, broken

voyage.name: 69 Manin Street B&B Rome
voyage.content: Cosy Bed and Breakfast of the historic centre of Rome with double, twin triple and quadruple rooms. Toilet with shower and breakfast included. €140 for a double. Same price for a double for single use.

voyage.name: Magnifico Hotel Rome
voyage.content: Budget accommodation with six bedrooms divided in single, double, quadruple and suites. All with private bath and modern facilities. Double: €130. Breakfast included.

voyage.name: Target Inn
voyage.content: A town house with 5 classic rooms, 1 deluxe and 1 suite, which can host up to four people. Modern facilities (plasma TV, internet ADSL), car parking, free breakfast, private bath and Jacuzzi bathtub.

voyage.name: Esposizione Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Hotel 3 Stars in the centre of Rome near Termini Station in front of Palazzo delle Esposizioni, exhibition centre.

voyage.name: Relais Trevi 41 Rome
voyage.content: The Relais Trevi 41 is a guest house with double and twin bedrooms. All with private bath and shower whirlpool.

voyage.name: Hotel Bernini Bristol
voyage.alt: A member of Summit Hotels and Resorts
voyage.content: Near the Spanish Steps and Trevi Fountain. All rooms come with an LCD flat-screen TV and WiFi access.

voyage.name: Residenza Borghese
voyage.content: A modern inn near Via Veneto.

voyage.name: Hotel Quirinale
voyage.content: 4 star hotel close to Piazza Repubblica. Style from the mid-19th century, reasonably large rooms and high ceilings. Internet connection costs €15 for 24 hours. Service at reception can be very poor, on occasions, it is downright rude.

voyage.name: Hotel Victoria Roma
voyage.content: 4 star hotel close to Via Veneto.

voyage.name: InterContinental Rome Ambasciatori Palace by IHG
voyage.content: Prestigious five-star hotel.

voyage.name: Villa Spalleti Trivelli
voyage.content: A splurge hotel in a quiet location. The rooms are large, with extra high ceilings, linens and bed of good quality, bath with shower and separate tub, bidet and two sinks. All the interiors are beautifully decorated, and the outside garden is perfect for a midday break. The staff is friendly and supportive.

voyage.name: Residenza Frattina
voyage.content: A clean, quiet and small hotel. Free internet in the spacious lounge. The rooms are not too big, but really comfortable. Good continental breakfast - a buffet of juices, toast, cereal and pastries. The staff is attentive and really helpful.

voyage.name: Baglioni Hotel Regina - Rome
voyage.content: 5-star hotel that features a mid-19th-century style, high ceilings, and reasonably spacious rooms. Breakfast is sometimes included in the rate.

voyage.name: The Pantheon
voyage.alt: Basilica of St. Mary and the Martyrs
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 08:00-19:30, Sun 09:00-18:00, public holidays 09:00-13:00, closed Jan 1, May 1, Dec 25
voyage.content: It was built in 27 BCE, by Augustus' right hand man Marcus Agrippa, and later remodeled by the Emperor Hadrian (AD 125-128). This ancient temple was built as a temple to all the gods of the Roman state but has served as a Christian church since the 7th century. It is the only building from the Graeco-Roman world which has remained substantially intact and in continuous use throughout to the present day, and as it is

voyage.name: Largo di Torre Argentina
voyage.content: Not, as commonly believed, named after the country but after the city of Strasbourg (Argentoratum in Latin), from which came a courtesan of Pope Alexander VI who lived nearby. Four Roman Republican-era temples, Pompey's theater and a Roman public toilet ("Latrina") have been excavated. The Pompey Theater is the site where Julius Caesar was stabbed to death by senators in 44 BC. The largo is also home to a large numbe

voyage.name: Temple of Hadrian
voyage.content: The temple of the Emperor Hadrian was consecrated in 145 AD by Emperor Antoninus Pius. The remains of the antique temple were incorporated into a new building that served as the Papal Customs House. It was finished around 1690 and today accommodates the Stock Exchange (Borsa).

voyage.name: Sant'Andrea della Valle
voyage.content: Minor basilica in 17th-century baroque style with good art inside. In a smaller Italian city, this might be a prime attraction, but in Rome, with its abundance of great churches, this is merely a pleasant church of secondary interest to visit if you are in the area.

voyage.name: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
voyage.content: This little church is hard to find but well worth the extra effort although it is often closed when you get there. One of Borromini's masterpieces. It is located only a block from Piazza Navona, but not usually visible from the street, as you must enter the courtyard of an old palazzo to reach the church. Sant'Ivo is a small church the dome of which is shaped like the Star of David, but with every other point rounded

voyage.name: Santa Maria sopra Minerva
voyage.content: This church is literally right next to the Pantheon. It is one of Rome's only Gothic churches, and well worth looking inside, although its plain square façade makes it look inconspicuous from outside. Excellent stained glass windows.

voyage.name: San Luigi dei Francesi
voyage.content: This church is roughly halfway between Piazza Navona and the Pantheon. It is most notable for a side chapel which contains three Caravaggio masterworks: "The Calling of St. Matthew", "St. Matthew and the Angel" and "Martyrdom of St. Matthew".

voyage.name: Sant'Ignazio
voyage.content: Between the Pantheon and Via del Corso. A stunning example of Baroque art. The ceiling frescoes are especially fine, including a trompe l'oeil dome by the master Andrea Pozzo.

voyage.name: Sant'Agnese in Agone
voyage.content: By Borromini, reputed to be on the spot where St. Agnes was martyred in the 4th century AD. This lovely basilica church is small with an almost circular interior. It is undergoing rehabilitation and the facade and dome are hidden in scaffolding. It seems to be open only until noon.

voyage.name: Santa Maria dell'Anima
voyage.content: Contains the tomb of Pope Adrian VI, the last non-Italian pope before Pope John Paul II.

voyage.name: Santa Maria della Pace
voyage.content: The church was built by order of Pope Sixtus VI (della Rovere). The campanile was erected in 1504 by Bramante and the church has frescoes of the four sibyls by Raphael in its interior.

voyage.name: Campo de' Fiori
voyage.content: If it is sunny, you'll catch a few young people and older gentlemen sitting at the base of a statue in the middle of the open space. The statue is a brooding, hooded Giordano Bruno—an excommunicated Dominican monk and one of the earliest cosmologists who held the idea of an infinite universe. He was burnt at the stake for heresy on this spot on 17 February 1600. The piazza is used as a marketplace during the day, and

voyage.name: Piazza Navona
voyage.content: The pride of Baroque Rome, was established towards the end of the 15th century, and preserves the shape of the ancient Stadium of Domitian. The buildings surrounding the square stand where the spectators once sat, watching the spectacle of the naumachiae (battles among ships). The square remains completely unspoilt by traffic and modern buildings. Today, the square is an immensely popular place to sip a cappuccino, s

voyage.name: Piazza Colonna
voyage.content: Where the building of the Italian Government, Palazzo Chigi is situated. Also there is a marvelous carved column—hence the name—dating back to Imperial Rome.

voyage.name: Piazza della Minerva
voyage.content: A small piazza just behind the Pantheon. The centerpiece is a statue of an elephant by Bernini with an ancient obelisk on its back.

voyage.name: Piazza di Sant'Ignazio
voyage.content: Small and attractive piazza tucked away in a neighborhood near Pantheon.

voyage.name: Piazza di Monte Citorio
voyage.content: Where you can find the building of the House of Representatives.

voyage.name: Piazza di Pasquino
voyage.content: Small piazza about 20 m (65 ft) from Piazza Navona, behind the Brazilian Embassy. There is a statue named "Pasquino", according to a legend named after a tailor who used to work nearby and had a reputation for complaining. The statue has been used for the past three centuries as a place to hang messages, complaints and other opinions which have to be shared with the neighborhood. The statue is probably an ancient Rom

voyage.name: Via Giulia
voyage.content: An example of urban planning that goes back to Pope Julius II, who, in 1508, envisioned it as a street that would connect all major government buildings. It is around a kilometer long and is in a straight line, an unusual feature for the time. It is lined with some interesting palaces but these days is more known for its antique shops. Via Giulia runs parallel with and one block from the River Tiber.

voyage.name: Via de Coronari
voyage.content: In the Middle Ages pilgrims on their way to St. Peter's had to pass through the Via dei Coronari in order to cross the Tiber at Ponte St. Angelo. The street got its name from the people who sold rosaries to the pilgrims. It follows the ancient Via Recta which led from what is today Piazza Colonna to the Tiber. In the 15th century Pope Sixtus IV initiated the construction of private buildings. Today, several houses da

voyage.name: Via del Governo Vecchio
voyage.content: The street is named after the Palazzo del Governo Vecchio, the seat of the Papal government in the 17th and 18th centuries. It was part of the Via papalis which connected St. John Lateran and St. Peter's. Houses nr. 104 and 106 date to the 15th century and there are some houses from the 16th century as well. The palace on nr. 123 was intended to be the residence of Bramante. The Palazzo del Governo Vecchio is situate

voyage.name: The Ghetto
voyage.content: The Ghetto lies between the island in the River Tiber and the Theatre of Marcellus and includes Rome’s synagogue. It was established in 1555 as a result of a Papal Bull by Pope Paul IV that required all Jews to live in the area, considered one of the least desirable quarters of the city, as it was subject to constant flooding by the river. The area was originally enclosed by walls and gates that were only open during

voyage.name: Palazzo della Cancelleria
voyage.content: This remarkable building served as the site of the Apostolic Chancellery, or offices of the Pope, for centuries, and now houses a Vatican court. Tucked behind the facade is also the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Damaso, an ancient Roman house church rebuilt in the 15th century.

voyage.name: Palazzo Farnese
voyage.content: Since 1871 this has been the French Embassy. This 16th-century palace contains an important fresco cycle by Annibale Carracci and houses a library of collections by the French school in Rome, particularly on Roman archaeology. Note the two beautiful fountains in the piazza.

voyage.name: Palazzo della Sapienza
voyage.content: This building housed the University of Rome from the middle of the 15th century until 1935. The splendid interior courtyard was created by Giacomo della Porta. The inside church of Sant'Ivo (see above) is one of the masterpieces of the architect Borromini.

voyage.name: Palazzo Altemps
voyage.alt: Branch of the Roman National Museum
voyage.price: €15 (less for EU citizens of ages 18-24) gives admission to this and the three other National Museums of Rome
voyage.content: Simple and elegant lines make up this building, whose construction began in 1480 for Count Girolamo Riario, nephew of Papa Sisto IV, and was taken up by architect Martino Longhi for the new owner, Cardinal Marco Sittico Altemps. Today it houses one of the branches of the National Museum of Rome, showcasing ancient and Renaissance sculptures, and the results of the 16th/17th-century fashion for 'completing' ancient sc

voyage.name: Palazzo Taverna
voyage.content: The building is in one of the most hidden corners of the city center among Piazza Navona and Castel Sant'Angelo. It served as residence for the Orsini family. Nowadays it is private property and one can only glance at the courtyard and the amazing fountain inside, erected in 1618 by architect Antonio Casoni. However, the brief moment is worth it.

voyage.name: Palazzo Crivelli
voyage.content: This building also known as the Doll House was built in the 16th century. It is unique for the quantity and quality of the decorations—lions' heads, satyrs and disfigured heads that adorn the facade attributed to the sculptor Giulio Mazzoni.

voyage.name: Palazzo Spada
voyage.content: This building was erected in the 16th century for Cardinal Girolamo Capodiferro. One century later it was acquired by another powerful Cardinal, Bernardino Spada, and was restored by Borromini, who created the forced perspective optical illusion in the arcaded courtyard.

voyage.name: Palazzo Madama
voyage.content: This palace of the 16th century was erected by the famous Medici family. It was the residence of Cardinals Giovanni and Giuliano Medici, later Pope Leo X. and Clement VII. Catherine de Medici, Pope Clement VII's niece lived here until her marriage in 1553 with Prince Henry, the son of King Francis I of France. The palace is named after Madama Margerita of Austria, the illegitimate daughter of Emperor Charles V. Since

voyage.name: Palazzo Massimo alle Colonne
voyage.content: The palace was built by the architect Baldassare Peruzzi on behalf of the Massimo family. The former palace was destroyed during the pillage of Rome in 1527. The Massimo family can be traced back to Quintus Fabius Maximus who defeated Hannibal in the 3rd century BC. The building is open to the public on March 16, only in order to commemorate the miraculous reanimation of Paolo Massimo by St. Philip Neri in 1538.

voyage.name: Palazzo del Collegio Romano
voyage.content: The Collegio Romano was a college of the Jesuit order. Many popes, cardinals and bishops were educated here. Since 1870 it has been a secular (non-monastic) school. The coat of arms on the doorway is that of Pope Gregory XIII (1572–1585). The tower was erected in 1787 and served as an observatory. Until 1925 all clocks in Rome were set after that of the Collegio Romano.

voyage.name: Hosteria dell'Orso
voyage.content: A historical inn where reputedly the Italian poet Dante Aligheri and French travellers of the 16th century, including the poets François Rabelais and Michel de Montaigne, stayed.

voyage.name: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi
voyage.content: By Bernini, in the very centre of Piazza Navona. Incorporates an Egyptian obelisk and symbolises four of the world's great rivers (the Ganges, the Nile, the Danube and the Plata), representing the four continents known at the time.

voyage.name: Fontana del Moro
voyage.content: At the southern end of the Piazza, designed by Bernini but the main statue of the Moor was done by Giacomo della Porta and the other statues are 19th-century copies of the originals.

voyage.name: Fontana del Nettuno
voyage.content: A 19th-century addition to the square, made to balance the Fontana del Moro.

voyage.name: Fontanella del Facchino
voyage.content: Like Pasquino, the Facchino is one of the so-called "speaking figures" which are peculiar to Rome. He is looking out of the Banco di Roma building. The man depicted is holding a barrel in his hands and is carrying water. It is sometimes said that he is looking similar to Martin Luther, but more probably a porter who died while carrying a barrel is depicted here.

voyage.name: Fontana delle Tartarughe
voyage.content: A pleasant fountain in an out-of-the-way square. It was originally meant to have four dolphins rather than turtles but the dolphins proved to be too large for the water pressure so the turtles were added as an afterthought.

voyage.name: Museo Napoleonico
voyage.content: The museum is dedicated to Napoleon Bonaparte and his family. After Napoleon's death in 1821 the Pope gave permission to his family to settle down in Rome. His sister married Prince Camillo Borghese.

voyage.name: Palazzo Altemps
voyage.alt: branch of the National Museum of Rome (Museo Nazionale Romano)
voyage.price: €10 adult, €6.50 EU citizens age 18-24 for access to all four National Museum of Rome sites
voyage.content: See Historical Buildings.

voyage.name: Crypta Balbi
voyage.alt: branch of the National Museum of Rome (Museo Nazionale Romano)
voyage.price: €10 adult, €6.50 EU citizens age 18-24 for access to all four National Museum of Rome sites
voyage.content: This museum is built on top of the excavation site of the Balbi Crypt, a building from the first century A.D. which underwent considerable modifications in the following centuries. Through the building's history, the museum gives us glimpses of what Roman life across the ages was like. Free visits of the ruins are possible. The Essedra ruins are only accessible on Saturdays and Sundays, at 10:45, 11:45, 12:45, 14:45

voyage.name: Obelisco di Montecitorio
voyage.content: An ancient Egyptian obelisk brought to Rome in 10 BC.

voyage.name: Santa Maria Minerva Obelisk
voyage.content: One of Bernini's masterpieces, an obelisk on the back of an elephant.

voyage.name: Pizzeria da Baffetto
voyage.content: Old-fashioned, family feel pizzeria near Piazza Navona and the Pantheon, unarguably serving some of the best pizzas in Rome. Usually crowded but well-worth the occasional queuing.

voyage.name: Pasta In Corso
voyage.content: There is another branch near the Pantheon, on Via della Maddalena, 43.

voyage.name: Alice
voyage.content: Part of an Italian chain serving pizza al taglio (square pieces to be eaten by hand), dozens of pizzas to choose from.

voyage.name: Cul de Sac
voyage.hours: Kitchen works until 01:00. In Aug, closed for 2 weeks
voyage.content: One of the best enoteche (wine bars) in Rome, serving a wide range of small dishes. The pate selection is a must-try. However, off-hours service is slow.

voyage.name: Il Bacaro
voyage.content: You'd never know that you are three minutes walk from Piazza Navona and the Pantheon. Via degli Spagnoli is tiny, leafy and quiet. Il Bacaro seats about 24 inside and even fewer outside under the shade of an ancient vine. Great selection of wine. In general a great stop for a romantic meal in the Eternal City.

voyage.name: La Taverna del Ghetto
voyage.content: Meat restaurant, excellent lamb dishes.

voyage.name: Tapa Loca
voyage.content: Spanish food.

voyage.name: Taverna Lucifero
voyage.content: A hole-in-the-wall Italian restaurant. As of summer 2012, not too crowded—it seems people haven't found it yet. All seating is inside. Don't miss the eggplant appetizer, mozzarella and tomato appetizer, limoncello liquor, tiramisu and chocolate mousse. Closes for entire month of August for holidays.

voyage.name: BellaCarne Kosher Grill
voyage.content: Focused on the world of kosher meats, bringing back Jewish traditions and culture to the heart of Rome’s Jewish neighbourhood, along with the typical tastes and recipes from Rome’s Jewish cuisine.

voyage.name: Forno di Campo de' Fiori
voyage.content: A traditional bread shop that makes one of the best kinds of pizza bread in Rome. With your back to the Giordano Bruno statue in the middle of the square, the Forno is at the bottom of the square to the left. Good place to have lunch.

voyage.name: Della Palma
voyage.content: Located just a couple blocks north of the Pantheon, this is an excellent gelateria with 140 different flavors. Prices are very reasonable. Vegan soy gelato also available.

voyage.name: Frigidarium
voyage.content: One of Rome's best artisanal gelaterias, but without the fussy attitude that marks some of the higher-class or more expensive locations. Excellent rotating flavors, all prepared on the spot. Their eponymous house flavor comes with a free cookie.

voyage.name: Gelateria Giolitti
voyage.content: It opened in 1800, and is very popular amongst locals, tourists. The late Pope John Paul II was known to be a regular customer. Among the best ice cream in Rome. About €4 for a large cup and €2 for a regular cone.

voyage.name: Vineria Reggio
voyage.content: Great place to sit for an affordable drink.

voyage.name: The Drunken Ship
voyage.content: Western bar. Nice for a quiet afternoon drink but are usually quite noisy at night, with specials most nights to encourage business. Girls are encouraged to have fun by lying on the bar and allowing guys to drink shots off their chests. Do not visit this bar on nights when England or English teams play football at Stadio Olimpico, because Italian lads often come here armed with knives to pick a fight.

voyage.name: Caffè Novecento
voyage.content: Offers a very good variety of cakes, sweets, coffee and tea. The furnishing are nice, with couches as seats at some tables. Prices are mid-high range but worth every cent.

voyage.name: Caffè Giolitti
voyage.content: An elegant coffee house in the style of the Belle Epoque, opened 1900. It offers among the best ice cream in Rome.

voyage.name: B&B Campo de'Fiori
voyage.content: Modern design in a building dating back to 1600. Non smoking rooms with A/C, tv, safe, free Wi-Fi. Private bathroom with shower.

voyage.name: Hotel Ponte Sisto
voyage.content: Peaceful and quiet, the 4-star Hotel Ponte Sisto in Rome is located in a completely renovated historic building, enveloped in a relaxing atmosphere with a splendid garden filled with luxuriant palm trees and flowers from all over the world.

voyage.name: Best Pantheon
voyage.content: A relatively new B&B with very modern decor. Four rooms with A/C, satellite TV, and DVD players + movies.

voyage.name: FortySeven Hotel
voyage.content: A modern hotel with quite spacious rooms, hot breakfast, nice fitness facility, and a rooftop restaurant/bar with gorgeous views. Walking distance to Trastevere.

voyage.name: Maison Giulia
voyage.content: Guesthouse near Campo de Fiori and Trastevere.

voyage.name: Hotel Portoghesi
voyage.content: Externally attractive hotel in a relatively quiet area of a busy part of town.

voyage.name: Hotel Raphael
voyage.content: Behind an ivy-covered facade on a narrow side street behind the Piazza Navona. The first floor houses a collection of Mayan art and original ceramics by Picasso; the third floor and its rooms were designed by Richard Meier. The restaurant is expensive but of very high quality. The (also expensive) rooftop terrace and bar is beautiful and has excellent views over the city, particularly of the Vatican.

voyage.name: Pantheon Royal Suite
voyage.content: A boutique hotel beside the Pantheon. Rooms are modern and comfortable with clean linens. The receptionists are friendly and helpful.

voyage.name: Residenza Frattina
voyage.content: Town House Hotel near the Vatican. Features 9 individual rooms with private bathrooms, decorated in classic Roman style. Tea and coffee maker, wi-fi internet, air conditioning, flat-screen satellite TV.

voyage.name: Passepartout
voyage.content: Small hotel/guest house, around 10 rooms with private bathrooms, air conditioning, wi-fi/internet, and TV.

voyage.name: Ara Pacis
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-19:00, 24 and 31 Dec 09:00-14:00; closed Mon, Jan 1, May 1 and Dec 25
voyage.content: Ara Pacis is an altar to peace commissioned by the Roman Senate on 4 July 13 BC to honor the triumphal return from Hispania and Gaul of Augustus. It is universally recognised as a masterpiece. Following discovery of this work under a building in Rome, Mussolini built a protective building for it near the Mausoleum of Augustus, where it was reconstructed. A new building on the same site as Mussolini's was opened in 20

voyage.name: Mausoleo di Augusto
voyage.content: This is a large tomb built by the Roman Emperor Augustus in 28 BC in the form of a stone ring covered by an earth mound. A brick wall, 87 m in diameter, carried an earth mound covered with cypresses. On top of the hill stood a bronze monument of the emperor. The building was 44 meters high. At the beginning of the alley, which led to the tomb were two Egyptian obelisks. On both sides of the doorway bronze plates desc

voyage.name: Catacombe di Priscilla
voyage.content: Underground burial place of an ancient Roman family and of seven early popes.

voyage.name: Santa Maria del Popolo
voyage.content: This is a treasure-trove of art. There are a couple of paintings by Caravaggio: "The Crucifixion of Saint Peter" and "The Conversion of Saint Paul" (in a dim alcove to the left of the altar, both at right angles to the viewer, with a machine wanting €2 to switch on the lighting) together with a sculpture by Bernini, frescoes by Pinturicchio and mosaics by Raphael. Part of the Dan Brown tour, this church featured in A

voyage.name: Santissima Trinità dei Monti
voyage.content: Baroque church more noted for its position at the top of the Spanish Steps than it is for the church. Backdrop for numerous movies including Audrey Hepburn and Gregory Peck in Roman Holiday.

voyage.name: Moschea di Roma
voyage.hours: Wed Sun 09:00-12:30 (excluding Ramadan, Italian holidays and August)
voyage.content: The Rome Mosque, which was inaugurated in 1995, is the biggest in Europe. The inside of the 30,000 m² structure has a large prayer hall that uses tri-stemmed columns that imitate the features of trees.

voyage.name: Santa Costanza
voyage.content: This church was built by the Emperor Constantine (272-337) as a mausoleum for his daughters Constantina and Helena. It was part of a much larger cemetery complex, parts of which can still be seen. The mausoleum was consecrated as a church and dedicated to Constantina when she became a saint in 1254. The building is circular with an inner arcade resting on pairs of granite columns. It retains some marvellous mosaics f

voyage.name: Sant' Agnese fuori le Mura
voyage.alt: Saint Agnes outside the walls, not to be confused with Sant' Agnese in Agone, to be found in Piazza Navona
voyage.content: This church was built next to the mausoleum of Santa Costanza in the 7th century and is on top of catacombs. It is very unusual in that the floor level is at the level of the catacomb floor, and the street entrance is at the level of the second floor gallery. The body of St. Agnes lies in a silver sarcophagus. There are several stories about her death at the age of 13 in 304 AD. One is that the prefect Sempronius wan

voyage.name: Catacombs of St Agnese
voyage.content: Small catacombs that contained the remains of Saint Agnes

voyage.name: Piazza del Popolo
voyage.content: This is the largest square in Rome. It sometimes hosts pop concerts and is the focal point for Rome's New Year's Eve celebrations. The twin churches Santa Maria dei Miracoli (1681) and Santa Maria in Montesanto (1679) used to provide a clear welcome to Rome for those coming from the north. Much older, to the north of the piazza is yet another Santa Maria (see below). The Piazza del Popolo is considered as one of the

voyage.name: Quartiere Coppedè (part of the neighborhood of ‘Trieste’)
voyage.content: With its strange Liberty- style buildings with influence from the Art Nouveau of the 1920s this small bunch of blocks is one of the most interesting, and less known, landmarks of the city. A must see.

voyage.name: The Spanish Steps
voyage.content: A truly monumental stairway of 135 steps (similar to climbing eight flights of stairs), built with French funds between 1721 and 1725 in order to link the Bourbon Spanish embassy to the Holy See (still located in the piazza below), with the Bourbon French church (its monastery founded in 1495) above. Don't sit on them though, or eat, or push a baby stroller on them, or do anything else that might obstruct pedestrians

voyage.name: Piazza di Spagna
voyage.content: The Piazza di Spagna (Spanish Square) is the most famous square in Rome. For a very long time it was the meeting point of all foreigners coming to Rome. In the 17th century it was the residence of the Spanish Ambassador to the Holy See. The area around the residence was Spanish territory and foreigners who stayed here without permission were forced to serve in the Spanish army. The Fontana della Barcaccia (Old Boat F

voyage.name: Ponte Milvio
voyage.content: The first pedestrian-only bridge was built here in 206 BC and marks the passage of the Roman Via Flaminia over the Tiber. In 115 BC, the original bridge was demolished and rebuilt. It has been restored and remodelled several times since. In 2006, the bridge began attracting couples who, influenced by a movie, used a lamppost on the bridge to hang padlocks as a sign of their love, locking the padlock to the lamppost,

voyage.name: Villa Medici
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:30 (ticket office); guided tour of gardens in English daily at 12:00
voyage.content: The villa was erected by order of Cardinal Ricci di Montepulciano in 1544. It was acquired by Cardinal Fernando di Medici in 1576. Since 1803 it is the French Academy in Rome. The academy was created in 1666 by the French King Louis XIV in order to enable painters to study in Rome. Nicolas Poussin was one of the first students, Ingres was director, and Fragonard and Boucher were students of the French Academy, but al

voyage.name: Villa Albani-Torlonia
voyage.content: A magnificent patrician house with beautiful gardens. It was built by order of Cardinal Alessando Albani in 1743-1763 in order to accommodate his collection of art. The collection was taken care of by the Winkelmann, adviser and friend of the cardinal. In Rome, Winkelmann wrote his "Geschichte der Kunst des Altertumns (HIstory of the Art of Antiquity)", which made him the founder of classical archaeology. The painted

voyage.name: Villa Ada
voyage.address: via Salaria 267 - 273 - 275, via di Ponte Salario, via di Monte Antenne, via Panama
voyage.content: Beautiful park, the 2nd largest in Rome (after Villa Doria Pamphili) at 450 acres/182 hectares. Hosts concerts on summer evenings. former summer residence of Italian monarchs. Also known for its bunker.

voyage.name: Borghese Gardens
voyage.content: The extensive Borghese Gardens are a pleasant place to stroll. Inside this area you will find one of the world's great museums, Rome's Zoo, a pond where you can rent a rowing boat and the Piazza di Siena, which hosts an annual show jumping event.

voyage.name: Pincio
voyage.content: The Pincio Park is near Piazza del Popolo. It was designed in the 19th century by Giuseppe Valadier, who also designed the Piazza del Popolo. Formlerly the Casina Valadier was an elegant restaurant. Gandhi, Mussolini, Richard Strauss and the Egyptian King Farouk were customers there. There are many evergreen bushes, palm and pine trees on both sides of the paths. Don't miss the view from Piazzale Napoleone I. to the

voyage.name: Monte Mario
voyage.content: The highest hill in Rome at 139 m, with sweeping views of the Vatican and Rome across the Tiber.

voyage.name: Villa Borghese
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 08:30-19:30 (mandatory exit at the end of allotted 2-hour slot, ticket office closes at 18:30)
voyage.address: Piazzale del Museo Borghese (Parco di Villa Borghese)
voyage.content: Borghese Gallery and Museum is a lovely display in a beautiful villa setting, which concentrates on the quality rather than the size of its collection. There are some very notable works by Antonio Canova and Gian Lorenzo Bernini here, Bernini's Apollo and Daphneis quite amazing. It also houses some of Caravaggio paintings, well worth the admission charge. Originally, the gallery was one of the most magnificent privat

voyage.name: Villa Giulia National Gallery
voyage.price: Full €8, concessions for students and pensioners
voyage.address: Piazzale di Villa Giulia, 9, Villa Borghese 00196 - Roma
voyage.content: The most extensive collection of Etruscan art and artifacts anywhere. Fantastic collection and well worth the admission charge. A difficult museum to find, but a lovely display in a beautiful villa setting.

voyage.name: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (GNAM)
voyage.alt: the National Gallery of Modern Art
voyage.content: An underrated way to see fantastic art made after the Renaissance. Mainly Italian artists, notably De Chirico, but Cézanne, Degas, Kandinsky, Man Ray, Modigliani, Monet, Pollock and Van Gogh are also represented.

voyage.name: MAXXI
voyage.alt: Museo Nazionale delle Arti del XXI Secolo (National Museum of 21st Century Art)
voyage.content: Brand new museum designed to celebrate the art and architecture of the 21st century.

voyage.name: MACRO
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:30-19:00 (last admission 1 hour before closing), Mon closed
voyage.content: Rome's museum of contemporary art, housed in a former industrial complex. Rotating exhibitions, each one usually lasting about 4 months. The MACRO Testaccio exhibition space is located in Aventino-Testaccio.

voyage.name: Keats-Shelley Memorial House
voyage.content: The house in which the famous English poet John Keats succumbed to consumption, now preserved as a memorial to his life and that of his friend Shelley, both of whom are buried in Rome's Protestant Cemetery (see Testaccio).

voyage.name: Goethe's House
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Mon closed (last admission 30 min before closing)

voyage.name: Museo delle Paste Alimentari
voyage.content: A museum devoted to pasta, Italy's premier gift to world cuisine.

voyage.name: Bioparco
voyage.hours: From 09:30 to 17:00 or 18:00 depending on the month
voyage.content: The renamed Rome Zoo, one of the oldest in Europe, founded in 1911. On the edge of the Borghese Gardens, a short, well-signposted walk from the Gallery. They try hard, but San Diego this isn't. If you are a regular zoo-goer you will be disappointed.

voyage.name: Piazza del Popolo Obelisk
voyage.content: According to an inscription Emperor Augustus dedicated the obelisk to the sun in the 11th year of his consulate (10BC), after he had annexed Egypt to Rome. The obelisk is 24 m high. It was erected in Heliopolis in Egypt and was dedicated to Pharao Sethos I (1313-1292 BC) and Pharoa Ramses II (1292-1275 BC). Augustus brought the obelisk to the Circus Maximus, where it was rediscovered in 1587, broken into three pieces

voyage.name: Statue of Lord Byron
voyage.content: Statue by Thorvaldsen.

voyage.name: Auditorium Parco della Musica
voyage.content: The Auditorium at Parco della Musica is a large complex on the north side of Rome, built on a site that was part of the 1960 Olympic area. It is composed of three separate halls whose shapes are inspired by musical instruments. These are positioned around an open air amphitheatre, that is used nearly every night in the summer for concerts. The interiors are entirely made of cherry-wood, which provides for good acoust

voyage.name: Il Margutta RistorArte
voyage.content: A fairly decent vegetarian lunch buffet. The staff can point out the vegan eats. A decent value for the money. Near where Fellini once lived.

voyage.name: Fiaschetteria Beltramme da Cesaretto
voyage.hours: Open for lunch and dinner. Closed Sun
voyage.content: Outdoor seating available. Cash only. Walls lined with interesting art and at least one communal table. Small, traditional menu but the best dishes are the pastas and the simple bresaola, rughetta and parmigiano plate. Recommended dishes are the tonnarelli cacio & pepe and maltagliati al sugo.

voyage.name: La Casa del Cremolato
voyage.content: One of the best Cafe of the area. Try the homemade cremolato, probably one of the best in Rome.

voyage.name: Caffè Vaticano
voyage.content: Delicious fruit gelato with exotic fruit bits, ice creams and coffees.

voyage.name: Osteria delle Commari
voyage.content: An Italian restaurant that does not do pizza. A little expensive.

voyage.name: Siciliainbocca
voyage.price: Reasonable prices; fish plate around €15, but do order some antipasti and pasta
voyage.content: Nice Sicilian restaurant in the quiet (and somewhat boring) part of northern Prati. Try the swordfish and the lemon sorbet!

voyage.name: Babington's Tea Rooms
voyage.content: situated right next to the base of the Spanish Steps, a veritable tourist trap. The cheapest pot of tea is €8. It opened in 1896 in order to fortify homesick English tourists, once famous as a tranquil English haven in a Latin ocean, now serving tea and scones (and more) with considerably less charm and even less value.

voyage.name: Antico Caffe Greco
voyage.content: In March 2026, it is closed due to a rent dispute. Ancient and famous coffee bar, with walls lined with art work. Worth a quick look even if you find the prices a bit excessive.

voyage.name: Babette caffe-ristorante
voyage.content: Lovely lunch buffet. Everything fresh out of the kitchen. Much more expensive on weekends. Always best to reserve. A nice way to sample lots of different Italian foods without having to order an antipasti, primi, secondi, etc.

voyage.name: Franklin Feel The Sound Hotel
voyage.content: Hotel with a unique music theme. The décor is very modern and stylish. Staff was helpful friendly and polite, continental breakfast is varied and plentiful. The rooms are clean, funky and very comfortable.

voyage.name: Filomena e Francesca B&B
voyage.content: Bed and Breakfast. Three rooms with private bathrooms and air-con.

voyage.name: Mocenigo Vatican Suites
voyage.content: Seven-room guesthouse 100 m from the main entrance to the Vatican Museums.

voyage.name: LH Excel Roma Montemario
voyage.address: via degli Scolopi 31, Montemario Area, zona Trionfale
voyage.content: This hotel has open air pool, restaurant, free parking and fitness center.

voyage.name: Hotel Cinquantatre
voyage.content: Hotel is in an old building with a roof-top terrace, rooms are with satellite TV, A/C and a safe, some with balcony as well.

voyage.name: Hotel Condotti
voyage.price: Single rooms from €136, double rooms from €175, triple rooms from €209, quadruple rooms from €223

voyage.name: Hotel Concordia
voyage.content: A hotel in an 18th-century building with A/C and a roof garden.

voyage.name: Imperial Suite Rome
voyage.price: €80/€95 single/double rooms. All rates include the breakfast served directly in the guests’ rooms
voyage.content: A guest house with single, double, twin and triple bedrooms. All with private bath, internet connection and living area.

voyage.name: PapavistaRelais
voyage.content: Guesthouse fairly close to the Vatican's main entrance.

voyage.name: Les Fleurs Luxury House
voyage.content: Cosy guest house with double and twin standard bedrooms €260, double deluxe, junior suite €380 and double for single use €230. All rates include breakfast and en-suites services with shower and bathtub or Jacuzzi.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn Rome Claridge
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in the Parioli district, close to the Borghese Gardens.

voyage.name: Hotel Lord Byron
voyage.price: single rooms from €190, double rooms from €225

voyage.name: B&B Domus Pinciana
voyage.content: Small B&B close to Via Veneto.

voyage.name: Intown Luxury House
voyage.content: Single, double, junior suite and terraced junior suite. All rooms with A/C, LCD TV sets with satellite channels, hi-speed Internet connection, safe, minibar and direct telephone line. Bathrooms are fitted with marble and Jacuzzi tubs and/or showers.

voyage.name: Best Western Astrid
voyage.content: A big hotel in a quiet area of Rome. The staff is friendly and makes the stay very enjoyable. The rooms are clean and spacious and there’s a daily replenishment of the minibar at no cost. The 5th-floor breakfast room has great views of the Tiber and St. Peter's Dome. The bar is closed at night and there isn't much nightlife in the area apart from a few good restaurants.

voyage.name: Spagna Royal Suite Rome
voyage.content: Boutique hotel. Double, triple and quadruple rooms divided in standard, comfort, deluxe and executive. All with private bath. Rates change according to the season, starting from £239 for a double standard and €399 for a triple deluxe.

voyage.name: Town House Spagna
voyage.content: Relatively new town house 50 m away from Piazza di Spagna. 10 rooms, each with private bathrooms. Up to date facilities.

voyage.name: c-hotels Fiume Roma
voyage.content: Nice hotel near the Villa Borghese park.

voyage.name: New Homs
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Stendhal
voyage.content: 4-star hotel.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Hotel Spring House
voyage.content: A small 3-star hotel with rooms that are a bit small, but comfortable and quiet. Great breakfast, wonderful service (maids and reception).

voyage.name: Hotel Museum Rome
voyage.content: Nice three-star hotel, 35 bedrooms with air conditioning and free Wi-Fi, large common area, complimentary breakfast, and terrace with panoramic view of the Roman roofs.

voyage.name: San Crisogono
voyage.content: Underneath the beautiful baroque church (with repurposed ancient Roman columns) there is a surprisingly large crypt, where ancient Roman ruins can be viewed. You can also see beautiful early Christian frescoes. Entry is €3 per person, payable in cash only.

voyage.name: Casa della Fornarina
voyage.content: There is little information available on Raphael's mistress La Fornarina. Margherita was the daughter of a baker from Siena. His shop was near Villa Farnesina where Raphael was painting. It is reported that Raphael repudiated her on his death bed as he wanted to be redeemed from his sins. Four months after his death Margherita joined the monastery Santa Apollonia in Trastevere. It is said that she was model for Rapha

voyage.name: Ponte Sisto
voyage.content: Pope Sixtus IV della Rovere (1471-1481) gave order to replace the old Roman bridge by a new one. It was Pope Sixtus IV who also ordered the Sistine Chapel and the Opsedale di Santo Spirito to be built. So he ran out of money. He levied a tax on prostitution in order to gain money for the construction of the Ponte Sisto.

voyage.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
voyage.content: One of the oldest churches in the city. The nave is lined with a mismatched collection of columns taken from ancient Roman buildings. The apse is covered in gold mosaics from the 13th century, arguably the finest mosaics in the city. Impressive mosaics also on the front. According to legend the church was founded in 222, so it would be one of the most ancient churches in the city. Written records mention a church on

voyage.name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
voyage.address: Piazza di Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
voyage.content: Very ornately done and beautiful inside, but don't expect any information in English. All information panels are only in Italian. It's still a beautiful site though even if you don't read Italian. According to tradition St.Cecily suffered a particular cruel death as a martyr. She was scalded, suffocated and beheaded by three strokes on her neck. As she was singing all the time during her martyrdom she is considered t

voyage.name: San Francesco a Ripa
voyage.hours: open to the public every day from 08:00 to 13:00 and from 14:00 to 19:30. During the liturgical celebrations is not possible to visit the church or the shrine
voyage.content: Named after St. Francis of Assisi, who stayed nearby. Inside the Paluzzi-Albertoni chapel is one of Bernini’s masterpieces, the statue of the Blessed Ludovica Albertoni. The column in front of the church comes from the ruins of Veii (see Rome/North).

voyage.name: Villa Farnesina
voyage.content: Delightful Renaissance house that was built by a rich banker from Siena, Agostino Chigi. In 1577 it was bought by the Farnese family and has since been known as Villa Farnesina. At one time there were plans by Michelangelo to build a bridge over the river to connect the villa with Palazzo Farnese on the other side. You can tour several beautiful rooms that are all decorated with frescoes, including some by Raphael. P

voyage.name: National Gallery of Ancient Art
voyage.content: housed in the baroque palace Corsini where Christina, Queen of Sweden settled down in the last years of her life

voyage.name: Orto Botanico dell'Università di Roma "La Sapienza"
voyage.content: This garden was established in 1883. It has over 3,500 species of plants and includes a "Scent-and-Touch" garden for those who are visually impaired.

voyage.name: Museum of Rome in Trastevere
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-20:00, Mon closed. Last admission 1h before closing
voyage.content: Permanent collection features paintings and drawings of Rome between the 18th and 20th centuries together with a fascinating black and white photo exhibition of Rome from 1950-80. Also offers rotating exhibitions, usually of the work of photographers.

voyage.name: Villa Sciarra
voyage.content: A lovely, if somewhat run-down park (parts of it are blocked due to the poor state of the roads) with statues and a great view on the city.

voyage.name: Il Gianicolo
voyage.content: This is not, contrary to popular belief, one of the original seven hills that Rome was founded on. It is the second highest after Monte Mario, though, and offers incredible panoramic views of the city as long as the authorities remember to prune the trees on the hillside (if they are too tall you can walk a few meters down the hill for views that are just as good). On the other side of the piazza there is also a nice

voyage.name: San Pietro in Montorio
voyage.content: This church, which was commissioned by Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain, marks the point where, according to tradition, St. Peter was crucified. Particularly interesting for Irish visitors as it contains the graves of three Gaelic Chiefs who fled Ireland in 1607.

voyage.name: The Tempietto
voyage.content: Designed by Bramante to mark the spot of St. Peter's martyrdom, this delightful miniature building is considered a masterpiece of Renaissance architecture. Open to the public.

voyage.name: Fontana dell'Acqua Paola
voyage.content: This massive early 17th-century Baroque fountain was built to celebrate the re-opening of an old Roman aqueduct. Water played an important role in this area in Roman times as the grain was milled here using water mills.

voyage.name: Manfredi Lighthouse
voyage.content: Strange to see a lighthouse on top of a hill. This was built in 1911 and was a gift to the city from Italians living in Argentina. From here you can continue down the hill, past Rome's largest and Italy's most important children's hospital, Bambino Gesu, eventually arriving at the River Tiber close to the Vatican.

voyage.name: Get lost in Trastevere
voyage.content: The cobbled streets are narrow and winding and random but losing your way will lead you to places you might not otherwise find. Note that the cobblestone streets (locally called sampietrini) are being paved elsewhere in Rome as the vibrations from cars driving over them have been found to lead to cracking in the foundations of many of the monuments and historic sites around the city. The sampietrini are mostly being

voyage.name: Piazza S. Maria in Trastevere
voyage.content: Beautiful place to hang around and watch people going by, as well as the many buskers usually found in the square. Join the students sitting on the steps of the fountain or, if you can afford it, have a drink or meal at one of the restaurants and bars on two sides of the square.

voyage.name: Big Mama
voyage.hours: Shows normally begin around 22:00 but check Press for details
voyage.address: Vicolo di San Francesco a Ripa 18
voyage.content: Rome’s original "House of the Blues". Has been going strong for 25 years. Italian and international artists, with blues and jazz concerts.

voyage.name: Porta Portese
voyage.content: On Sunday mornings there is a huge flea market. It extends from Porta Portese to Viale di Trastevere.

voyage.name: Ai Bozzi
voyage.content: Italian restaurant with excellent food and professional service. Traditional dishes as well innovative variations (try the fettuccine with artichokes and guanciale). Pizza is also served in the evening. Lovely outside terrace overlooking the piazza.

voyage.name: Augusto
voyage.content: A small osteria in the heart of Trastevere. Authentic non-touristic Roman restaurant serving classic Roman dishes, hand-made desserts and wine. It's a good idea to phone ahead to see if they have room because this small place fills up fast every night, although if you don't mind waiting they'll squeeze you in if they can. They do not take reservations.

voyage.name: Fior di luna
voyage.content: Very good ice cream and made from fair trade products by an ice cream artist with a passion for taste.

voyage.name: Glass Hostaria
voyage.content: Uber-modern trattoria.

voyage.name: Ivo a Trastevere
voyage.address: Via di S. Francesco a Ripa 158
voyage.content: Get here early if you want a table without a wait. Very popular pizzeria that attracts lengthy queues of young Romans, so it must be good.

voyage.name: La Gattabuia
voyage.content: Serves pizza, pasta and steak. Great atmosphere and friendly staff. Unique location and décor.

voyage.name: Osteria dell'Aquila
voyage.content: Mediterranean style restaurant. Menu is in Italian and English, and the waiters speak both languages. Open for lunch and dinner. The meals here are excellent and at very good prices. Make sure to try the seafood appetizers.

voyage.name: Osteria der Belli
voyage.content: Run by four brothers from Sardinia. Particularly recommended for its seafood dishes.

voyage.name: Pizzeria La Boccaccia
voyage.address: Via di San Francesco a Ripa 21
voyage.content: Great little pizzeria run by 2 friendly Neapolitan brothers. You can get a big slice and a huge ice cold beer for €5. The place gets full of locals. That should tell you everything. get there quite early as in the evening they have a few pizzas left, most popular time is around lunch and after school. Also note that the street Via di San Francesco a Ripa has a strange numbering system - odd and even numbers are on th

voyage.name: Il Vicola Da Tony
voyage.content: On a beautiful old Roman laneway with indoor and outdoor seating. One of the best lasagne in the city as well as plenty of pasta, meat and seafood options. Risotto alla pescatora (seafood risotto) is delicious; don't ask for the fish if you can't get a quick mortgage to pay for it. Prices bear no relation whatsoever to the menu.

voyage.name: Trattoria de Gli Amici
voyage.content: Very interesting place in the heart of Trastevere district. Run by very kind handicapped people, it has nice cuisine.

voyage.name: Vincenzo alla Lungaretta
voyage.content: Out of the way. Great food and great service and a very reasonable price.

voyage.name: Vivi Bistrot
voyage.content: Suitable for children as well. Useful for arranging a picnic in the park.

voyage.name: Enoteca Ferrara
voyage.content: Luxury restaurant

voyage.name: Sora Lella
voyage.hours: closed Sun, Tue morning and 2 weeks in August

voyage.name: Baccanale
voyage.content: A small bar with a great range of drinks, friendly staff and a manic display of cocktail making later on in the evening. There are several TV screens showing major sporting events. Probably the best bar in the world considering its location and stereotypical perfection. The staff are very welcoming to tourists. It is a secret that you'll be lucky to find in the narrow, winding streets of Trastevere.

voyage.name: Hotel Cisterna Rome
voyage.content: 2-star hotel with 24-hr reception. 20 rooms, All equipped with modern services and private bathrooms. Bookable online.

voyage.name: Roma Trasteverina B&B
voyage.price: Single €40-60, double €80-120, twin and double rooms

voyage.name: Relais Rome Sweet Home Trastevere
voyage.content: Small hotel with 4 rooms. All equipped with satTV, Wi-Fi and private bathrooms. Online booking.

voyage.name: Arco dei Tolomei
voyage.content: All the rooms come with private bath and shower.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Gianicolo Rome
voyage.content: Four star accommodation with twin, double with jacuzzi, triple and dus (double for single use). All with private bath and shower. Swimming pool, a private garden and a fantastic panoramic view of Rome.

voyage.name: Hotel Santa Maria
voyage.content: Gated hotel just off Piazza Santa Maria. Comfortable and has a nice courtyard.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa della Fonte
voyage.content: Small hotel, all rooms have a private bath, free Wi-Fi, satelliteTV and A/C.

voyage.name: WRH Trastevere
voyage.content: Friendly modern & minimalist guesthouse.

voyage.name: Gran Meliá Rome
voyage.content: A luxury 5-star hotel with single, double, triple and quadruple rooms, very quiet with a view of Vatican City.
